### Discord username (optional)

*No response*

### Describe the solution you'd like?

Playing around, I enabled the Emacs bindings, which are still incomplete. M-b and M-f still don't do what I expected (move backward and forward by words).

All terminals use readline to support this. It gives the Emacs bindings and VI-Style bindings optional.

So instead of asking for "completing the Emacs bindings", I think the wise thing to do is to fully support [readline](https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/readline.3.html).

### Describe the bug

`ctrl+y` does "delete all left" on linux and you need to unbind it for paste from internal clipboard to work. 

meaning by default I don't see any easy way to paste from internal clipboard (therefore commands like `ctrl+u` are useless by default)

### To reproduce

1. put some text into the terminal field
2. pres ctrl+y -> it will delete the test to the left)
3. clear the ctrl+y binding
4. put some text into the field again
5. press ctrl+u
6. press ctrl+y -> it will paste from internal buffer (what ctrl+u deleted)

### Expected behavior

At least warn a user about this in some way. 
Or let user change the internal "hard-coded" bindings.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

_No response_

Linux

fixedbinding for yank: https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/blob/c37c1cd6ec75726ea297131bab2b2b0b19ecce60/app/src/editor/view/mod.rs#L266

labels.name: enhancement

items.body:
### Describe the solution you'd like?

```shell
In order to make sure that you can copy on-screen text in any mode, add button which while being pressed allows to select any text with mouse on terminal screen as-is (and copy it to buffer).

E.g on Mac in iTerm you can select any on screen by pressing [Option] key - that works for Vim & all other cases as well
```


### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

```shell
Normally you can select any part of on-screen text and copy it to system buffer.

When having Vim with `set mouse=a` it becomes impossible to select text in terminal screen since vim intercepts selection & turns on visual mode. So no way you can just select-and-copy select without diving into vim yanking.
```

items.title: Custom keybindings or missing keyboard shortcuts? Or Vim mode? Emacs? See here! (bindings / bind / bindable)
items.body:
We'll share major progress updates in this issue! So please subscribe (GitHub watch)

See the Custom Keybindings GitHub Discussion to report bugs and workarounds. This helps us keep it all in one place.
- https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/discussions/500

Try to use this precedence when referring to the keybindings: CTRL-ALT-SHIFT-CMD-KEY

Here's a summary of current requests and whether we've fulfilled them.

non-key
- [ ] leader key (like tmux)

bugs
- [ ] ESC -> in theme selector should exit
- [ ] ESC -> in font selector should exit

misc
- [ ] ENTER -> Ability to configure whether enter executes command or inserts new line (CMD-ENTER to run)
- [ ] ALT -> in alt-screens to bypass mouse selection (vim)
- [ ] ALT-. -> iterate over the arguments of prior commands
- [x] ALT-LEFT -> move word left
- [x] ALT-RIGHT -> move word right
- [x] ALT-CMD-DOWN -> multi-cursor down
- [x] ALT-CMD-UP -> multi-cursor up

items.title: KB: Ctrl + U/K doesn't cut to clipboard
items.body:
**Describe the bug**
`Ctrl + U` clears the text, but does not put it in the clipboard, so a subsequent `Ctrl + Y` pastes something different.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
Type a bunch of text, press `Ctrl + U`, press `Ctrl + Y`

**Expected behavior**
Cut text is pasted back into terminal.

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
 - OS Version: [e.g. MacOS 11.5]

items.title: Neovim (with plenty of plugins) performance slower than expected
items.body:
### Describe the solution you'd like?

```shell
I would like vim/neovim performance with highly configured setups to perform as fast as other competing terminal applications.
```


### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

```shell
Neovim performance, especially with lots of plugins, is considerably slower than almost every other Terminal application (Alacritty, MacOs Terminal, etc.)

One of the main reasons I use a terminal is for Neovim, and I imagine many other terminal users use customized vim/neovim configurations. 

This definitely surprised me, as with every other application I have not noticed any other performance issues.
```
